title: Plan it or wing it?

hosts.Leyla: lives in Baku and loves a good plan
hosts.Sam: grew up in Manchester and once travelled with no plan at all

voiceDirection: The SpeakLab Podcast: two friendly hosts recording in a cosy studio. Warm, smiling, unhurried. Clear articulation for B1 learners, about 130 words a minute, natural pauses between turns. Real chemistry, light laughter, never rushed.

before.predict: Do you plan every day of a trip, or do you just go? Guess: who is the planner — Leyla or Sam?

chapters.title: Planner or not?
chapters.prompt: SCENE: a backpacker with a huge rucksack on a mountain road in South America at sunrise, a paper map in hand, small and alone in a wide landscape

chapters.title: Airport stories
chapters.prompt: SCENE: a busy airport at night, a tired traveller asleep on a row of chairs during a long layover, a departures board glowing, a boarding pass sticking out of a jacket pocket

chapters.title: Tips for your next trip
chapters.prompt: SCENE: one small carry-on bag, a water bottle and an open notebook with a short simple plan, a sunny window with a city outside, calm and light

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is one of my favourites: travel.
Mine too. So, Sam, a simple question to start. When you travel, do you plan everything, or do you just hit the road?
[chuckle] Honestly? I used to plan nothing. When I was twenty, I was a backpacker in South America for three months. No hotels, no plan. Just a big bag and a map.
Three months! Weren't you homesick?
Oh, very. By week two I missed my mum's cooking so much. But I learned a lot.
I'm the opposite. I love an itinerary. Before a trip, I write down every day: where we go, what we eat, what time the museum opens.
Every day? That sounds like a lot of sightseeing.
[laugh] It is! And sometimes it's too much. Last year in Rome I saw so many famous places that I was exhausted.
That's why I like places off the beaten track. A small village, a quiet café, no tour buses.
That sounds lovely. Okay, but here's the part of travel I really hate: airports.
Ah, yes. The long queues at customs...
...and the moment you can't find your boarding pass. [sigh] It's always in the last pocket.
[laugh] Always. And what about a long layover? Last month I had nine hours in Doha.
Nine hours! What did you do?
I slept on a chair. Not my best idea. And then I had terrible jet lag for three days.
My tip for jet lag: drink lots of water, go outside in the daylight, and don't sleep in the afternoon.
Good advice. And here's mine: travel light. One small bag. You move faster, and you never wait for your suitcase.
I'm trying! It's hard for me. [short pause] So, let's sum up. Plan a little, but leave some space for surprises.
Exactly. The best memories are often the things you didn't plan.
Now it's your turn. In your next SpeakLab call, ask your partner: what was your best trip, and what went wrong?
Have fun with it. See you next time!
Bye for now!
